function.name: get_users_list
function.description: Retrieve a comprehensive list of all users in the Slack workspace including their profiles, roles, and status information. Essential for user management, team analysis, and understanding workspace demographics. Use this to get detailed information about workspace members, identify admins and bots, or analyze user activity patterns.

cursor.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata

include_locale.description: Set this to true to receive the locale for users

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned, even if the end of the users list hasn't been reached

team_id.description: encoded team id to list users in, required if org token is used

function.name: get_user_info
function.description: Retrieve detailed information about a specific user in the Slack workspace including their profile, status, and workspace permissions. Essential for user lookup, profile management, and understanding individual user capabilities. Use this to get specific user details, check user status, or verify user permissions.

include_locale.description: Set this to true to receive the locale for this user

function.name: get_user_profile
function.description: Retrieve a user's profile information including their display name, status, title, and other profile fields. Essential for profile management and user information display. Use this to get detailed profile data for a specific user.

function.name: set_user_profile
function.description: Update a user's profile information including display name, status, title, and other profile fields. Essential for profile management and user customization. Use this to update user profile data, set status messages, or modify user information.

profile.description: Collection of key:value pairs presented as a URL-encoded JSON hash

name.description: Name of a single key to set

value.description: Value to set a single key to

function.name: admin_users_assign
function.description: Assign a user to channels (admin function). Essential for user management and channel administration. Use this to assign users to specific channels, manage channel memberships, or organize team structure.

user_id.description: The user to assign to channels

channel_ids.description: List of channel IDs to assign the user to

function.name: admin_users_invite
function.description: Invite a user to the workspace (admin function). Essential for user onboarding and workspace growth. Use this to invite new users to the workspace, manage invitations, or expand team membership.

team_id.description: The ID (e.g., 'T1234') of the workspace.

email.description: The email address of the person to invite. Example: joe@email.com

channel_ids.description: A comma-separated list of channel IDs for this user to join. At least one channel is required. Example: C1A2B3C4D,C26Z25Y24

custom_message.description: Optional message to include in the invite email. Example: Come and join our team!

real_name.description: Full name of the user. Example: Joe Smith

resend.description: Allow this invite to be resent later via the UI if the user hasn't signed up yet (default: false).

is_restricted.description: Is this user a multi-channel guest user? (default: false)

is_ultra_restricted.description: Is this user a single channel guest user? (default: false)

guest_expiration_ts.description: Timestamp when the guest account should be disabled (only for guest users). Example: 0123456789.012345

email_password_policy_enabled.description: Allow invited user to sign in via email and password (Enterprise Grid only). Example: true

function.name: admin_users_remove
function.description: Remove a user from the workspace (admin function). Essential for user management and workspace administration. Use this to remove users from the workspace, manage departures, or maintain workspace security.

team_id.description: The team/workspace ID

barriered_from_usergroup_ids.description: A list of IDP Groups ids that the primary usergroup is to be barriered from (e.g., ['S03TNHGAUGZ'])

app_id.description: The ID of the app to associate with this datastore entry (optional)

function.name: apps_datastore_update

app_id.description: The ID of the app to query datastore entries for (required)

limit.description: Maximum number of items to return (optional)

function.name: apps_connections_open

function.name: get_channels_list

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination from previous response_metadata

exclude_archived.description: Exclude archived channels from the list

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Recommended ≤200, max 1000

team_id.description: Team ID to list channels in (required for org-level tokens)

types.description: Comma-separated list of channel types: public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im

function.name: get_conversations_history
function.description: Retrieve message history for a specific channel including messages, timestamps, and metadata. Essential for message analysis, conversation tracking, and communication history. Use this to get message history, analyze conversations, or retrieve specific messages.

channel.description: Channel ID to get history for (required)

cursor.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata

inclusive.description: Include messages with latest or oldest timestamp in results

oldest.description: Start of time range of messages to include in results

function.name: users_conversations

cursor.description: Paginate through collections of data by setting the cursor parameter to a next_cursor attribute returned by a previous request's response_metadata

exclude_archived.description: Set to true to exclude archived channels from the list

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned, even if the end of the list hasn't been reached. Must be an integer with a max value of 999

team_id.description: Encoded team id to list conversations in, required if org token is used

types.description: Mix and match channel types by providing a comma-separated list of any combination of public_channel, private_channel, mpim, im

user.description: Browse conversations by a specific user ID's membership. Non-public channels are restricted to those where the calling user shares membership

function.name: chat_post_message
function.description: Post a message to a specific channel. Sends messages to public/private channels or DMs. Rate limits: 1 msg/sec per channel, several hundred/min per workspace. channel.description: Channel ID (C...), DM ID (D...), Group ID (G...), or User ID (U...) for DMs. Cannot use usernames. Use channel IDs from conversations.list or users.list. (required)

blocks.description: Structured blocks for rich message formatting (JSON array). Either text, blocks, or attachments must be provided

attachments.description: Structured message attachments (JSON array, deprecated in favor of blocks). Either text, blocks, or attachments must be provided

thread_ts.description: Timestamp of another message's ts value to make this message a reply

reply_broadcast.description: Used in conjunction with thread_ts to broadcast reply to entire channel

unfurl_links.description: Pass true to enable unfurling of primarily text-based content

unfurl_media.description: Pass false to disable unfurling of media content

icon_emoji.description: Emoji to use as the icon for this message

icon_url.description: URL to an image to use as the icon for this message

link_names.description: Find and link channel names and usernames

mrkdwn.description: Disable Slack markup parsing by setting to false (default: true)

metadata.description: JSON object with event_type and event_payload fields for message metadata

function.name: chat_delete
function.description: Delete a message from a conversation. Essential for message management, content moderation, and maintaining clean conversation history. Use this to remove inappropriate messages, fix mistakes, or clean up conversation threads. Only messages that the authenticated user can delete in Slack can be deleted.

channel.description: Channel containing the message to be deleted (required)

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to be deleted (required)

function.name: chat_delete_scheduled_message
function.description: Delete a pending scheduled message from the queue before it is sent. Essential for managing scheduled content, preventing unwanted messages, and maintaining control over automated communications. Use this to cancel scheduled messages, update communication plans, or manage content scheduling.

channel.description: The channel the scheduled_message is posting to (required)

scheduled_message_id.description: scheduled_message_id returned from call to chat.scheduleMessage (required)

as_user.description: Pass true to delete the message as the authed user with chat:write:user scope

function.name: chat_get_permalink
function.description: Retrieve a permalink URL for a specific extant message. Handles message threads and all conversation types. Rate limit: Hundreds of requests per minute allowed.

channel.description: The ID of the conversation or channel containing the message

message_ts.description: A message's ts value, uniquely identifying it within a channel

function.name: chat_me_message
function.description: Sends a me message to a channel from the calling user. This creates a message that appears in italics, similar to typing /me in Slack. Required scopes: chat:write

channel.description: Channel to send message to. Can be a public channel, private group or IM channel. Can be an encoded ID, or a name (e.g., #general)

text.description: Text of the message to send

function.name: chat_post_ephemeral
function.description: Send an ephemeral message to a user in a channel. Essential for private notifications, contextual help, and user-specific information delivery. Use this to send private messages visible only to specific users, provide contextual assistance, or deliver personalized notifications without disrupting the conversation flow.

channel.description: Channel, private group, or IM channel to send message to (required)

user.description: id of the user who will receive the ephemeral message (required)

text.description: Text of the message to send

blocks.description: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string

attachments.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string

icon_emoji.description: Emoji to use as the icon for this message

icon_url.description: URL to an image to use as the icon for this message

link_names.description: Find and link channel names and usernames

parse.description: Change how messages are treated. Defaults to none

thread_ts.description: Provide another message's ts value to post this message in a thread

function.name: chat_schedule_message
function.description: Schedules a message to be sent to a channel. Requires chat:write scope. Can schedule up to 120 days in future. Max 30 messages per 5 minutes to same channel. WARNING: Messages with metadata parameter won't post (known bug). Returns scheduled_message_id for tracking.

channel.description: Channel, private group, or DM channel to send message to. Can be an encoded ID, or a name

post_at.description: Unix timestamp representing the future time the message should post to Slack. Max 120 days in future

text.description: Message text. When blocks/attachments are included, used as fallback text for notifications only

blocks.description: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string

attachments.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string

link_names.description: Find and link user groups. No longer supports linking individual users

parse.description: Change how messages are treated. Defaults to 'none'

reply_broadcast.description: Used with thread_ts. Whether reply should be visible to everyone in channel. Defaults to false

thread_ts.description: Provide another message's ts value to make this message a reply. Avoid using a reply's ts; use its parent

unfurl_links.description: Pass true to enable unfurling of primarily text-based content

unfurl_media.description: Pass false to disable unfurling of media content

function.name: chat_scheduled_messages_list
function.description: Returns a list of pending scheduled messages. Essential for managing scheduled content, reviewing upcoming messages, and maintaining communication schedules. Use this to view pending scheduled messages, manage content calendars, or audit automated communications. All parameters are optional.

channel.description: The channel of the scheduled messages

cursor.description: For pagination purposes, this is the cursor value returned from a previous call

latest.description: A Unix timestamp of the latest value in the time range

limit.description: Maximum number of original entries to return (default 100)

oldest.description: A Unix timestamp of the oldest value in the time range

team_id.description: Encoded team id to list channels in, required if org token is used

function.name: chat_unfurl
function.description: Provide custom unfurl behavior for user-posted URLs. Essential for rich link previews, custom content display, and enhanced user experience. Use this to create custom previews for links, display rich content, or provide additional context for shared URLs. Either provide channel and ts, or unfurl_id and source

channel.description: Channel ID of the message. Both channel and ts must be provided together, or unfurl_id and source must be provided together

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to add unfurl behavior to

unfurls.description: URL-encoded JSON map with keys set to URLs featured in the message, pointing to their unfurl blocks or message attachments (required)

user_auth_message.description: Provide a simply-formatted string to send as an ephemeral message to the user as invitation to authenticate further

user_auth_required.description: Set to true or 1 to indicate the user must install your Slack app to trigger unfurls for this domain

user_auth_url.description: Send users to this custom URL where they will complete authentication in your app to fully trigger unfurling

user_auth_blocks.description: Provide a JSON based array of structured blocks presented as URL-encoded string to send as an ephemeral message

unfurl_id.description: The ID of the link to unfurl. Both unfurl_id and source must be provided together, or channel and ts must be provided together

source.description: The source of the link to unfurl. The source may either be composer, when the link is inside the message composer, or conversations_history

function.name: chat_update
function.description: Updates a message. Only messages posted by the authenticated user are able to be updated. Bot users must set as_user=true when updating their own messages. Ephemeral messages cannot be updated. OAuth scope required: chat:write.

channel.description: Channel containing the message to be updated. For direct messages, ensure that this value is a DM ID (starts with D) instead of a User ID

ts.description: Timestamp of the message to be updated

text.description: New text for the message. Limited to 12,000 characters. Used as fallback text for notifications when blocks or attachments are provided

blocks.description: A JSON-based array of structured blocks, presented as a URL-encoded string. If not provided, previous blocks retained only if text not provided

attachments.description: A JSON-based array of structured attachments, presented as a URL-encoded string

as_user.description: Pass true to update the message as the authed user. Bot users must set this to true when updating their own messages

file_ids.description: Array of new file IDs that will be sent with this message, presented as a URL-encoded JSON array

link_names.description: Find and link channel names and usernames. Defaults to none. If not specified, original value overwritten with default 'none'

metadata.description: JSON object with event_type and event_payload fields, presented as a URL-encoded string. Include empty object to remove previous metadata

parse.description: Change how messages are treated. Defaults to client. Accepts either none, full, or client

reply_broadcast.description: Broadcast an existing thread reply to make it visible to everyone in the channel or conversation

function.name: reactions_add
function.description: Adds a reaction (emoji) to a message. Essential for user engagement, feedback collection, and conversation interaction. Required scopes: reactions:write. Use this to add emoji reactions to messages, provide quick feedback, or mark messages with status indicators.

channel.description: Channel where the message to add reaction to was posted (required). Example: C1234567890

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the message to add reaction to (required). Example: 1234567890.123456

name.description: Reaction (emoji) name to add. For Unicode emoji with skin tone modifiers, use format like 'thumbsup::skin-tone-3' where skin tone is 2-6 (required). Example: thumbsup, white_check_mark, heart

function.name: reactions_get
function.description: Gets reactions for an item (message, file, or file comment). Returns a list of all reactions for a single item. Essential for retrieving reaction data, analyzing engagement, and understanding user feedback. Required scopes: reactions:read. Use this to get reactions on messages, files, or file comments. Either give channel and timestamp, or file, or file_comment

channel.description: Channel where the message to get reactions for was posted. Required when getting reactions for a message. Example: C1234567890

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the message to get reactions for. Required when channel is provided. Example: 1234567890.123456

file.description: File to get reactions for. Example: F1234567890

file_comment.description: File comment to get reactions for. Example: Fc1234567890

full.description: If true always return the complete reaction list. Default: false

function.name: reactions_list
function.description: Lists reactions made by a user. Returns a list of all items (file, file comment, channel message, group message, or direct message) with reactions made by the authenticated user or specified user. Required scopes: reactions:read. Use this to view all reactions made by a user, track user engagement, or analyze reaction patterns. Returns up to 1000 items with pagination support.

count.description: Number of items to return per page.

cursor.description: Parameter for pagination. Set cursor equal to the next_cursor attribute returned by the previous request's response_metadata.

full.description: If true always return the complete reaction list.

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Fewer than the requested number of items may be returned.

page.description: Page number of results to return.

team_id.description: encoded team id to list reactions in, required if org token is used.

user.description: Show reactions made by this user. Defaults to the authed user.

function.name: reactions_remove
function.description: Removes a reaction (emoji) from an item (message, file, or file comment). Essential for removing inappropriate reactions, correcting mistakes, or managing reaction-based workflows. Required scopes: reactions:write. Use this to remove emoji reactions from messages, files, or file comments. Must specify item using one of: file, file_comment, or channel+timestamp combination. Either give channel and timestamp, or file, or file_comment

name.description: Reaction (emoji) name to remove. For Unicode emoji with skin tone modifiers, use format like 'thumbsup::skin-tone-3' where skin tone is 2–6 (required). Example: thumbsup, white_check_mark, heart.

channel.description: Channel where the message to remove reaction from was posted. Required when using channel+timestamp identification. Example: C1234567890.

timestamp.description: Timestamp of the message to remove reaction from. Required when channel is provided. Example: 1234567890.123456.

file.description: File to remove reaction from. Alternative to channel+timestamp. Example: F1234567890.

file_comment.description: File comment to remove reaction from. Alternative to channel+timestamp or file. Example: Fc1234567890.

function.name: search_all

count.description: Number of items to return per page. Default is 20

highlight.description: Pass a value of true to enable query highlight markers

page.description: Page number of results to return. Default is 1

sort.description: Return matches sorted by either score or timestamp

highlight.description: Pass a value of true to enable query highlight markers

sort.description: Return matches sorted by either score or timestamp

sort_dir.description: Change sort direction to ascending ('asc') or descending ('desc')

team_id.description: The team_id is only relevant when using an org-level token. This field will be ignored if the API call is sent using a workspace-level token

function.name: conversations_create

team_id.description: Team ID

function.name: conversations_decline_shared_invite
function.description: Decline a shared channel invite. Essential for shared channel administration and invitation management. Use this to decline shared channel invitations or manage external collaboration requests.

function.description: Close a direct message or multi-person direct message. Essential for conversation management and cleanup. Use this to close DM or MPIM conversations. Only works on direct messages and multi-person direct messages, not regular channels.

function.name: conversations_info
function.description: Retrieve information about a conversation including metadata, member count, and settings. Essential for conversation analysis and channel management. Use this to get detailed information about channels, understand channel settings, or analyze conversation structure.

function.name: conversations_kick

channel.description: Channel ID to rename (required)

function.name: conversations_request_shared_invite_deny
function.description: Deny a request to invite an external user to a channel. Essential for shared channel administration and request management. Use this to deny external user requests, manage shared channel access, or control cross-workspace collaborations.

message.description: Optional message explaining why the request to invite was denied

function.name: conversations_request_shared_invite_list

function.name: conversations_set_topic
function.description: Set the topic of a conversation/channel. Essential for channel management, organization, and quick identification. Use this to update channel topics, set clear channel subjects, or maintain concise channel descriptions for better team communication and navigation.

channel.description: The ID of the channel to set topic for (required)

topic.description: The new topic for the channel (required, max 250 characters)

function.description: Unarchive a conversation/channel. Essential for channel lifecycle management and workspace restoration. function.name: admin_emoji_add

function.name: admin_emoji_list
function.description: List all custom emojis for an Enterprise Grid organization. This allows you to retrieve a comprehensive list of emojis available across the organization, including their names and URLs. Essential for emoji management, auditing, and understanding the organization's emoji collection.

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be between 1 - 1000 both inclusive

function.name: admin_emoji_remove
function.description: Remove a custom emoji from an Enterprise Grid organization. This allows you to delete emojis that are no longer needed or appropriate for the organization. Essential for emoji management and maintaining a clean, professional emoji collection.

name.description: The name of the emoji to be removed. Colons around the value are not required, although they may be included.

function.name: admin_emoji_rename
function.description: Rename a custom emoji across an Enterprise Grid organization. This allows you to change emoji names to be more descriptive, fix typos, or standardize naming conventions. Essential for emoji management and maintaining organized emoji collections.

name.description: The name of the emoji to be renamed. Colons around the value are not required, although they may be included.

new_name.description: The new name for the emoji. Must be lowercase and unique.

function.name: admin_functions_list
function.description: List all functions in a workspace or enterprise. This allows you to retrieve a comprehensive list of functions available in the workspace, including their configurations, execution statistics, and metadata. Essential for function management, monitoring, and understanding the workspace's function ecosystem.

app_ids.description: Array of app IDs to get functions for (max 50)

team_id.description: The team context to retrieve functions from

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page

limit.description: The number of results that will be returned by the API on each invocation

function.name: admin_functions_permissions_lookup
function.description: Lookup permissions for a specific function in a workspace or enterprise. This allows you to retrieve detailed information about the permissions required and granted for a function, including permission descriptions, scopes, and grant status. Essential for function security management, permission auditing, and understanding function access requirements.

function_ids.description: An array of function IDs to get permissions for

function.name: admin_functions_permissions_set
function.description: Set permissions for a specific function in a workspace or enterprise. This allows you to grant or update permissions for a function, control function visibility, and manage user access. Essential for function deployment, permission management, and security configuration.

function_id.description: The ID of the function to set permissions for

user_ids.description: List of user IDs to allow for named_entities visibility. Required when visibility is 'named_entities'

function.name: admin_inviteRequests_approve
function.description: Approve a workspace invite request. This allows administrators to approve pending invite requests from users who want to join the workspace. Essential for workspace access management and user onboarding.

invite_request_id.description: ID of the request to invite

team_id.description: ID for the workspace where the invite request was made

function.name: admin_inviteRequests_deny
function.description: Deny a workspace invite request. This allows administrators to reject pending invite requests from users who want to join the workspace. Essential for workspace access management and security.

invite_request_id.description: ID of the request to deny

team_id.description: ID for the workspace where the invite request was made

function.name: admin_inviteRequests_list
function.description: List all pending workspace invite requests. This allows administrators to view and review pending invite requests from users who want to join the workspace. Essential for workspace access management and monitoring.

cursor.description: Value of the next_cursor field sent as part of the previous API response

limit.description: The number of results that will be returned by the API on each invocation. Must be between 1 - 1000, both inclusive

team_id.description: ID for the workspace where the invite requests were made

function.name: admin_inviteRequests_approved_list
function.description: List all approved workspace invite requests. This allows administrators to view and review approved invite requests and their associated invites. Essential for workspace access management, audit trails, and understanding invite history.

cursor.description: Value of the next_cursor field sent as part of the previous API response

limit.description: The number of results that will be returned by the API on each invocation. Must be between 1 - 1000, both inclusive

team_id.description: ID for the workspace where the approved invite requests were made

function.name: admin_inviteRequests_denied_list
function.description: List all denied workspace invite requests. This allows administrators to view and review denied invite requests and understand rejection patterns. Essential for workspace access management, audit trails, and understanding invite rejection history.

cursor.description: Value of the next_cursor field sent as part of the previous API response

limit.description: The number of results that will be returned by the API on each invocation. Must be between 1 - 1000, both inclusive

team_id.description: ID for the workspace where the denied invite requests were made

function.name: admin_roles_addAssignments
function.description: Add role assignments to users for specified entities. This allows administrators to assign roles to users for specific teams, organizations, or channels. Essential for role-based access control, permission management, and administrative operations in Enterprise Grid organizations.

entity_ids.description: A list of entity IDs for which roles will be assigned. These can be Org IDs (starting with 'E'), Team IDs (starting with 'T'), or Channel IDs (starting with 'C')

role_id.description: ID of the role to which users will be assigned. Must be one of the valid role IDs (e.g., 'Rl01' for Channel Admin, 'Rl03' for User Admin)

user_ids.description: A list of user IDs to be added to the given role. User IDs must start with 'U'

function.name: admin_roles_listAssignments
function.description: List role assignments for all roles across entities. This allows administrators to view and manage role assignments across teams, organizations, and channels. Essential for role-based access control auditing, permission management, and administrative oversight in Enterprise Grid organizations.

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page

entity_ids.description: A list of entity IDs for which the roles apply (e.g., ['T123ABC456', 'E123ABC456'])

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be between 1 - 200 both inclusive

role_ids.description: A list of role IDs to scope results by (e.g., ['Rl01', 'Rl03'])

sort_dir.description: Sort direction. Default is descending on date_create, can be either ASC or DESC

function.name: admin_roles_removeAssignments
function.description: Remove role assignments from users for specified entities. This allows administrators to revoke role assignments from users for specific teams, organizations, and channels. Essential for role-based access control management, permission revocation, and administrative oversight in Enterprise Grid organizations.

entity_ids.description: A list of entity IDs for which roles will be revoked (e.g., ['T123ABC456', 'E123ABC456', 'C123ABC456'])

role_id.description: ID of the role from which users will be removed (e.g., 'Rl01', 'Rl03')

user_ids.description: A list of user IDs whose roles will be revoked (e.g., ['U123ABC456', 'U789DEF012'])

function.name: admin_teams_create
function.description: Create an Enterprise team. This Admin API creates a workspace for an enterprise organization. Essential for enterprise workspace management, team provisioning, and organizational structure setup. Use this to create new teams within an Enterprise Grid organization.

team_domain.description: Team domain (e.g., slacksoftballteam). Domains are limited to 21 characters

team_discoverability.description: Who can join the team: 'open', 'closed', 'invite_only', or 'unlisted' (optional)

function.name: admin_teams_list
function.description: List all teams on an Enterprise organization. This Admin API lists workspaces in an enterprise organization. Essential for enterprise workspace management, team discovery, and organizational oversight. Use this to get an overview of all teams within an Enterprise Grid organization.

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page (optional)

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be a positive integer no larger than 1000 (optional, default: 100)

function.name: admin_teams_owners_list
function.description: List all of the owners on a given workspace. This Admin API method returns a list of the owners for a given workspace. Essential for team ownership management, administrative oversight, and understanding team hierarchy. Use this to identify who has owner permissions for a specific team.

team_id.description: The team ID to list owners for (required)

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page (optional)

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be between 1 - 1000 both inclusive (optional, default: 100)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_info
function.description: Fetch information about settings in a workspace. This Admin API method fetches information about settings in a workspace. Essential for workspace configuration management, settings overview, and administrative control. Use this to retrieve team settings, configuration details, or workspace information.

team_id.description: The team ID to get settings for (required)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_set_default_channels
function.description: Set the default channels of a workspace. This Admin API method sets the default channels of a workspace. Default channels are joined by new members of a workspace automatically. Essential for workspace configuration management, onboarding automation, and team structure setup. Use this to configure which channels new members will automatically join.

team_id.description: ID for the workspace to set the default channel for (required)

channel_ids.description: An array of channel IDs to set as default channels (required)

function.name: admin_teams_admins_list
function.description: List all of the admins on a given workspace. This Admin API method returns a list of the admins for a given workspace. Essential for team administration management, permission oversight, and understanding team admin hierarchy. Use this to identify who has admin permissions for a specific team.

team_id.description: The team ID to list admins for (required)

cursor.description: Set cursor to next_cursor returned by the previous call to list items in the next page (optional)

limit.description: The maximum number of items to return. Must be between 1 - 1000 both inclusive (optional, default: 100)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_set_description
function.description: Set the description of a given workspace. This Admin API method sets the description of a given workspace. Essential for workspace branding, documentation, and team identity management. Use this to update workspace descriptions for better organization and clarity.

team_id.description: ID for the workspace to set the description for (required)

description.description: The new description for the workspace (required)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_set_discoverability
function.description: Set the discoverability of a given workspace. This Admin API method sets the discoverability of a given workspace. Essential for workspace privacy and access control management. Use this to control who can find and join the workspace.

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to set discoverability on (required)

discoverability.description: This workspace's discovery setting. It must be set to one of 'open', 'invite_only', 'closed', or 'unlisted' (required)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_set_icon
function.description: Set the icon of a given workspace. This Admin API method sets the icon of a given workspace. Essential for workspace branding and visual identity management. Use this to update workspace icons for better organization recognition and branding.

team_id.description: ID for the workspace to set the icon for (required)

function.name: admin_teams_settings_set_name
function.description: Set the name of a given workspace. This Admin API method sets the name of a given workspace. Essential for workspace branding and identity management. Use this to update workspace names for better organization recognition and clarity.

team_id.description: ID for the workspace to set the name for (required)

name.description: The new name of the workspace (required)

function.name: admin_usergroups_add_channels
function.description: Add one or more default channels to an IDP group. This Admin API adds one or more default channels to an IDP group. Essential for managing user group access to channels and ensuring proper communication channels are available to group members. Use this to configure default channels for user groups, manage group access permissions, or set up communication workflows.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the IDP group to add default channels for (required)

channel_ids.description: Comma separated string of channel IDs (required)

team_id.description: The workspace to add default channels in (optional)

function.name: admin_usergroups_add_teams
function.description: Add one or more teams to an IDP group. This Admin API adds teams to an IDP group, enabling the usergroup to be available across multiple workspaces. Essential for managing user group availability across teams and ensuring proper access control in multi-workspace environments. Use this to configure team access for user groups, manage cross-workspace permissions, or set up organization-wide user groups.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the IDP group to add teams to (required)

team_ids.description: A comma separated string of encoded team (workspace) IDs. Each workspace must belong to the organization associated with the token (required)

auto_provision.description: When true, this method may auto-provision a usergroup on the given teams (optional)

function.name: admin_usergroups_list_channels
function.description: List channels associated with an IDP group. This Admin API retrieves the list of channels that are associated with a specific usergroup. Essential for understanding user group channel access, managing group permissions, and auditing channel associations. Use this to review channel access for user groups, verify group configurations, or generate reports on usergroup channel associations.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the IDP group to list channels for (required)

include_num_members.description: Include the number of members in each channel (optional)

team_id.description: The workspace to list channels in (optional)

function.name: admin_usergroups_remove_channels
function.description: Remove one or more default channels from an IDP group. This Admin API removes default channels from an IDP group, enabling fine-grained control over user group channel access. Essential for managing user group permissions, restricting access to specific channels, and maintaining security policies. Use this to revoke channel access for user groups, update group configurations, or implement access control policies.

usergroup_id.description: ID of the IDP group to remove default channels from (required)

channel_ids.description: Comma separated string of channel IDs (required)

function.name: admin_users_set_admin
function.description: Set a user as admin for a workspace. This Admin API designates a user as an admin for a specific workspace, granting them administrative privileges and access to workspace management features. Essential for workspace administration, user management, and access control. Use this to promote users to admin status, manage workspace permissions, or delegate administrative responsibilities.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to designate as an admin (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to set the user as admin for (required)

function.name: admin_users_set_expiration
function.description: Set an expiration date for a user's account in a workspace. This Admin API allows setting a timestamp when a user's account should expire, enabling automated account lifecycle management. Essential for user access control, compliance requirements, and temporary access management. Use this to set account expiration dates, manage temporary users, or implement access time limits.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to set expiration for (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to set expiration for (required)

expiration_ts.description: Timestamp when the user's account should expire (required)

function.name: admin_users_set_owner
function.description: Set a user as the owner of a workspace. This Admin API designates a user as the workspace owner, granting them full administrative privileges and ownership rights. Essential for workspace ownership transfer, administrative hierarchy management, and organizational control. Use this to transfer workspace ownership, establish primary administrators, or manage workspace governance.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to designate as the owner (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to set the user as owner for (required)

function.name: admin_users_set_regular
function.description: Set a user as a regular user in a workspace. This Admin API removes admin and owner privileges from a user, downgrading them to regular user status. Essential for privilege management, security control, and administrative hierarchy adjustments. Use this to revoke administrative access, manage user permissions, or implement role-based access control.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to set as regular (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to set the user as regular for (required)

function.name: admin_users_session_clear_settings
function.description: Clear session settings for a user in a workspace. This Admin API removes all session-related settings for a user, resetting them to default values. Essential for session management, security control, and user session troubleshooting. Use this to reset user session configurations, clear session preferences, or resolve session-related issues.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to clear session settings for (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to clear session settings for (required)

function.name: admin_users_session_get_settings
function.description: Get session settings for a user in a workspace. This Admin API retrieves all session-related settings for a user, providing detailed information about their session configuration. Essential for session management, security monitoring, and user session analysis. Use this to review user session configurations, monitor session settings, or troubleshoot session-related issues.

function.name: admin_users_session_invalidate
function.description: Invalidate user session in a workspace. This Admin API terminates a user's active session, forcing them to re-authenticate. Essential for security control, session management, and emergency access termination. Use this to terminate compromised sessions, enforce security policies, or manage user access during security incidents.

user_id.description: ID of the user that the session belongs to (required)

session_id.description: ID of the session to invalidate (required)

team_id.description: ID of the workspace that the session belongs to (optional)

function.name: admin_users_session_list
function.description: List user sessions in a workspace. This Admin API retrieves all active and inactive sessions for a user, providing detailed information about their session history and current activity. Essential for session monitoring, security analysis, and user activity tracking. Use this to review user session history, monitor active sessions, or investigate user activity patterns.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to list sessions for (required)

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to list sessions for (required)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page (optional)

limit.description: Maximum number of sessions to return (optional, default: 100, max: 1000)

function.name: admin_users_session_reset
function.description: Reset user session in a workspace. This Admin API resets a user's session, clearing session data and forcing re-authentication. Essential for session management, security control, and session troubleshooting. Use this to resolve session issues, clear session data, or force users to re-authenticate with fresh sessions.

user_id.description: The ID of the user to reset session for (required)

mobile_only.description: Only reset mobile sessions (optional, default: false)

web_only.description: Only reset web sessions (optional, default: false)

function.name: admin_users_session_reset_bulk
function.description: Reset user sessions in bulk for multiple users in a workspace. This Admin API resets sessions for multiple users simultaneously, clearing session data and forcing re-authentication. Essential for bulk session management, security control, and enterprise-wide session troubleshooting. Use this to resolve session issues for multiple users, clear session data in bulk, or force multiple users to re-authenticate with fresh sessions.

user_ids.description: The list of up to 1,000 user IDs to wipe sessions for (required)

mobile_only.description: Only expire mobile sessions (optional, default: false)

web_only.description: Only expire web sessions (optional, default: false)

function.name: admin_users_session_set_settings
function.description: Set user session settings in a workspace. This Admin API configures session parameters for a user, including timeout, duration, idle timeout, remember me settings, re-authentication requirements, and concurrent session limits. Essential for session policy management, security configuration, and user experience customization. Use this to configure session behavior, set security policies, or customize user session parameters.

user_ids.description: The list of up to 1,000 user IDs to apply the session settings for (required)

duration.description: The session duration in seconds (min 28800, max 315569520)

desktop_app_browser_quit.description: Terminate the session when the desktop app or browser is closed

function.name: admin_users_unsupported_versions_export
function.description: Request an export of users using unsupported software. The export is processed asynchronously and delivered by Slackbot. Provide optional timestamps to filter sessions and end-of-support cycles.

date_sessions_started.description: Unix timestamp to start looking for user sessions (optional)

date_end_of_support.description: Unix timestamp for past/upcoming end of support cycles (optional)

function.name: admin_users_list
function.description: List users in a workspace. This Admin API retrieves a comprehensive list of all users in a workspace, including detailed user information, profiles, and status. Essential for user management, administration, and workspace overview. Use this to get a complete view of workspace users, manage user accounts, or generate user reports.

team_id.description: The ID of the workspace to list users for (required)

cursor.description: Pagination cursor for the next page (optional)

is_active.description: Whether to return only active users (optional)

include_deactivated_user_workspaces.description: Whether to include deactivated user workspaces (optional)

only_guests.description: Whether to return only guest users (optional)

limit.description: Maximum number of users to return (optional, default: 100, max: 1000)

function.name: admin_workflows_collaborators_add
function.description: Add collaborators to a workflow. This Admin API adds users as collaborators to a specific workflow, enabling them to view, edit, or manage the workflow depending on their permission level. Essential for workflow collaboration, team management, and workflow administration. Use this to grant workflow access to team members, manage workflow permissions, or enable collaborative workflow development.

collaborator_ids.description: List of user IDs to add as collaborators (required)

function.name: admin_workflows_collaborators_remove
function.description: Remove collaborators from a workflow. This Admin API removes users as collaborators from a specific workflow, revoking their access to view, edit, or manage the workflow. Essential for workflow access control, team management, and workflow administration. Use this to revoke workflow access from team members, manage workflow permissions, or restrict workflow access.

collaborator_ids.description: List of user IDs to remove as collaborators (required)

function.name: admin_workflows_permissions_lookup
function.description: Look up permissions for which users are authorized to run workflows. This Admin API looks up permissions for which users are authorized to run workflows in the org. Since workflows themselves do not have an execution policy, the rule exists on the trigger associated with the workflow. Essential for workflow access control, permission management, and workflow administration. Use this to check who can run workflows, verify workflow permissions, or audit workflow access.

workflow_ids.description: The IDs of the workflows to lookup permissions for (required)

max_workflow_triggers.description: Maximum number of workflow triggers to check (optional, default: 100)

function.name: admin_workflows_search
function.description: Search for workflows in the workspace. This Admin API searches for workflows based on various criteria such as workflow IDs, app IDs, creator IDs, and other filters. Essential for workflow discovery, management, and administration. Use this to find specific workflows, list workflows by criteria, or audit workflow usage.

query.description: A search query to filter for workflow name or description (optional)

app_id.description: The parent app ID for which to return workflows (optional)

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination (optional)

limit.description: Maximum number of workflows to return (optional)

no_collaborators.description: Only include workflows with no collaborators in the result; default is false (optional)

collaborator_ids.description: List of collaborator IDs to filter by (optional)

num_trigger_ids.description: The number of trigger IDs to filter by; default is 10 (optional)

is_sales_elevate.description: Filter workflows by their Sales Elevate status (optional)

source.description: Source of workflow creation, either from code or workflow builder (optional)

sort.description: The field used to sort the returned workflows (optional)

trigger_type_id.description: Only include workflows with this trigger type ID (optional)

publish_status.description: Filter workflows by their publish status (optional)

step_function_ids.description: Only include workflows that use all of the provided step function ids (optional)

function.name: admin_workflows_unpublish
function.description: Unpublish a workflow (make it private). This Admin API unpublishes a workflow, making it private and no longer accessible to users outside of the workflow's collaborators. This is useful for restricting access to workflows that should no longer be publicly available. Essential for workflow access control, privacy management, and workflow administration. Use this to make workflows private, restrict workflow access, or manage workflow visibility.

workflow_id.description: The ID of the workflow to unpublish (required)

function.name: admin_workflows_triggers_types_permissions_lookup
function.description: Look up permissions for workflow trigger types. This Admin API looks up permissions for workflow trigger types in the organization. It provides information about what permissions are required for each trigger type and which channels they can be used in. Essential for workflow development, permission management, and trigger configuration. Use this to understand trigger permissions, configure workflow triggers, or audit trigger access.

trigger_type_ids.description: The trigger types IDs for which to get the permissions.

function.name: admin_workflows_triggers_types_permissions_set
function.description: Set permissions for workflow trigger types. This Admin API sets permissions for workflow trigger types in the organization. It allows administrators to configure what permissions are required for each trigger type and which channels they can be used in. Essential for workflow administration, permission management, and trigger configuration. Use this to configure trigger permissions, update access controls, or manage workflow security.

id.description: The trigger type ID for which to set the permissions

user_ids.description: List of user IDs to allow for named_entities visibility

function.name: files_remote_add
function.description: Register an externally hosted file with Slack so it can be referenced in conversations without uploading the binary. Ideal for surfacing documents stored in third-party systems while keeping Slack aware of their metadata.

external_id.description: Unique identifier provided by the remote file service (required).

external_url.description: Fully-qualified HTTP or HTTPS URL pointing to the remote file (required).

title.description: Title to display for the remote file inside Slack (required).

filetype.description: Optional file type hint such as 'pdf', 'docx', or 'image'.

indexable_file_contents.description: Optional plain-text contents that should be indexed for search within Slack.

preview_image.description: Optional base64-encoded preview image representing the remote file.

function.name: files_remote_list
function.description: List remote files that have been registered with Slack, using a limit-offset cursor so you can page through results deterministically. Ideal for auditing content mirrored from external repositories or syncing metadata across systems.

cursor.description: Base64-encoded offset cursor returned in response_metadata.next_cursor. Use this to fetch the next page.

limit.description: Maximum number of remote files to return per page.

channel.description: Restrict results to files visible in a specific channel (mock implementation accepts but ignores this filter).

ts_from.description: Return files created at or after this Unix timestamp.

ts_to.description: Return files created at or before this Unix timestamp.

function.name: files_remote_remove
function.description: Remove a previously registered remote file using either its Slack file ID or the provider's external identifier. Useful for cleaning up stale metadata when documents are retired upstream.  Either file or external_id must be provided.

function.name: files_remote_update
function.description: Update remote file metadata such as title, URL, or indexing contents using either the Slack file ID or provider external ID. Either file or external_id must be provided.

file.description: Slack remote file ID (cannot be modified by this call).

external_id.description: Provider-specific identifier originally supplied during registration.

external_url.description: Updated absolute HTTP or HTTPS URL for the remote file.

title.description: Updated title shown in Slack clients.

filetype.description: Updated file type hint such as 'pdf' or 'docx'.

indexable_file_contents.description: Updated plain text contents for search indexing.

function.name: files_remote_info
function.description: Retrieve metadata for a remote file previously registered with Slack. Use this to confirm file details, obtain the Slack file ID, or inspect indexing status for external content.  Either external_id or file must be provided.

external_id.description: Provider-specific identifier originally supplied when the file was registered.

function.name: files_comments_delete
function.description: Delete an existing comment on a file. Only the original author of the comment or a Team Administrator may delete a file comment. This method is part of the legacy file comments API that was deprecated in favor of file threads.

file.description: File ID containing the comment to delete (e.g., 'F1234567890').

function.name: files_delete
function.description: Delete a file from your team. This method deletes a file from your team. Note: this method works as expected on tombstoned files. Only the file owner or a Team Administrator may delete a file.

function.name: files_info
function.description: Get information about a file in your team, including file details and associated comments. Supports both traditional page-based and cursor-based pagination for comments. Bot user tokens may use this method to access information about files appearing in the channels they belong to.

file.description: File ID to get info for (e.g., 'F1234567890').

count.description: Number of comments to return per page (max 1000). Used with page parameter for traditional pagination.

page.description: Page number of results to return (max 100). Used with count parameter for traditional pagination.

cursor.description: Cursor for pagination. Used with limit parameter for cursor-based pagination (preferred).

limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return (max 1000). Used with cursor parameter for cursor-based pagination.

function.name: files_list
function.description: List files within the team. Can be filtered and sliced in various ways including by channel, user, file types, and time ranges. The team_id parameter is only relevant when using an org-level token and will be ignored for workspace-level tokens. Use show_files_hidden_by_limit to gather information on tombstoned files in Free workspaces.

channel.description: Filter files by channel ID.

count.description: Number of items to return per page (default 100, max 1000).

page.description: Page number of results to return (default 1).

show_files_hidden_by_limit.description: Show files hidden by limit in Free workspaces to gather tombstoned file IDs for deletion/revocation.

team_id.description: Team ID (only relevant when using org-level token, ignored for workspace tokens).

ts_from.description: Filter files created after this Unix timestamp.

ts_to.description: Filter files created before this Unix timestamp.

types.description: Filter by file types (comma-separated). Options: all, spaces, snippets, images, gdocs, zips, pdfs, or specific file extensions.

user.description: Filter files by user ID who created them.

function.name: files_get_upload_url_external
function.description: Get a URL that can be used for uploading a file to share within channels. The URL allows clients to send file data to Slack's file upload service. length.description: Size in bytes of the file being uploaded (e.g., 53072).

filename.description: Name of the file being uploaded (e.g., 'laughingoutloudcat.jpg').

function.name: files_complete_upload_external

id.description: File ID from the upload process.

files.description: Array of file ids and their optional titles.

channel_id.description: Channel ID where the file will be shared.

thread_ts.description: Provide parent's ts to upload as a reply.

channels.description: Comma-separated string of channel IDs where the file will be shared.

initial_comment.description: The message text introducing the file in specified channels.

blocks.description: JSON-based array of structured rich text blocks, URL-encoded.

function.name: files_remote_share

channels.description: Comma-separated list of channel IDs where the file will be shared (e.g., 'C1234567890,C0987654321'). Required.

external_id.description: External ID of the remote file to share (e.g., 'ABCD1234').

file.description: File ID registered with Slack (e.g., 'F2147483862'). Optional, but either this or external_id must be provided.

test.description: If true (aka 1), run in testing mode and do not actually revoke. If provided but not true, return an error.

function.name: auth_teams_list
function.description: List all workspaces (teams) your org-ready app is approved for. Supports pagination via cursor, limit (≤1000), and optionally includes icon URIs.

limit.description: Max number of workspaces to return (1..1000). Default: 100

cursor.description: Opaque cursor from response_metadata.next_cursor

include_icon.description: Whether to include an icon URI for each team. Default: false

function.name: auth_test
function.description: Check authentication and return identity context (team, user, url).

function.name: dnd_end_dnd
function.description: Ends the caller's currently scheduled Do Not Disturb (DND) session immediately.

function.name: dnd_end_snooze
function.description: Ends the current user's snooze mode immediately and returns DND state.

function.name: dnd_info
function.description: Provides information about a user's current Do Not Disturb settings.

user.description: User ID to fetch status for (defaults to the current user).

team_id.description: Team ID where the user belongs. Required if using an org token, or when no user is provided.

function.name: dnd_set_snooze
function.description: Adjust (or start) the current user's DND snooze for N minutes from now.

num_minutes.description: Number of minutes (from now) to snooze until (e.g., '60').

function.name: dnd_team_info
function.description: Get current Do Not Disturb schedule for a list of users in a team.

users.description: Comma-separated list of users to fetch Do Not Disturb status for

team_id.description: Team ID context. Required if using an org token; otherwise defaults to the authed user's team.

function.name: canvases_create
function.description: Create a canvas for a user

title.description: Title of the newly created canvas.

document_content.description: Structure describing the type and value of the content to create.

channel_id.description: Channel ID of the channel the canvas will be tabbed in. This is a required field for free teams..

function.name: canvases_edit
function.description: Edit a canvas

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas to edit

changes.description: Structure describing the changes to apply to the canvas

function.name: canvases_delete
function.description: Delete a canvas

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas to delete

function.name: canvases_sections_lookup
function.description: Find sections of a canvas matching the provided criteria

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas to lookup

criteria.description: Filtering criteria to use in looking up sections

function.name: slack_lists_items_info
function.description: Retrieve a single record (row) from a Slack List. Returns all fields, metadata, and optional subscription info.

list_id.description: ID of the List containing the record (e.g., 'F1234567').

id.description: ID of the row (record) to retrieve (e.g., 'Rec014K005UQJ').

include_is_subscribed.description: Include 'is_subscribed' data for the record. Default: false.

function.name: slack_lists_update
function.description: Update a Slack List’s name, description, and todo_mode settings.

id.description: The ID of the List to update.

name.description: The updated name of the List.

description_blocks.description: Rich text description blocks for the List.

todo_mode.description: Enable or disable todo mode for the List.

function.name: slack_lists_access_set
function.description: Set the access level to a Slack List for specified users or channels. Supports read, write, and owner levels.

list_id.description: Encoded ID of the List (e.g., F1234ABCD).

access_level.description: Desired access level for the List.

channel_ids.description: List of channel IDs to grant access to. Cannot be used with user_ids.

user_ids.description: List of user IDs to grant access to. Cannot be used with channel_ids.

function.name: slack_lists_access_delete
function.description: Revoke access to a Slack List for specified users or channels. Cannot provide both channel_ids and user_ids.

list_id.description: Encoded ID of the List (e.g., F1234ABCD).

channel_ids.description: List of channel IDs to revoke access from. Cannot be used with user_ids.

user_ids.description: List of user IDs to revoke access from. Cannot be used with channel_ids.

function.name: canvases_access_set
function.description: Sets the access level to a canvas for specified entities

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas to set access on

channel_ids.description: List of channels you wish to update access for. Can only be used if user_ids is not provided.

user_ids.description: List of users you wish to update access for. Can only be used if channel_ids is not provided.

parameters.NOTE: The user ID which registered a canvas has automatic `owner` scope which can initially set/delete other scopes

function.name: canvases_access_delete
function.description: Sets the access level to a canvas for specified entities

canvas_id.description: ID of the canvas to set access on

channel_ids.description: List of channels you wish to delete access for.

user_ids.description: List of users you wish to delete access for.

parameters.NOTE: The user ID which registered a canvas has automatic `owner` scope which can initially set/delete other scopes

function.name: apps_activities_list
function.description: Fetch logs and activity data for a given app. This method retrieves detailed execution and workflow logs, filterable by log level, event type, or component. Use it to monitor app events, debug workflows, or analyze execution history.

app_id.description: The ID of the app whose activities should be listed (required).

team_id.description: Optional team ID that owns this log.

limit.description: The maximum number of activity entries to return (default 100).

min_log_level.description: Minimum log level to include (trace, debug, info, warn, error, fatal).

trace_id.description: Trace ID to filter correlated logs.

min_date_created.description: Earliest timestamp (epoch microseconds) of logs to retrieve.

max_date_created.description: Latest timestamp (epoch microseconds) of logs to retrieve.
